**Visual analysis of the test image:**
- Severely distorted, narrow, and curling leaves with a "fern-leaf" appearance
- Extreme leaf distortion at growing tips — leaves elongated and filiform
- Mosaic pattern visible (light/dark green mottling on some leaves)
- Multiple stems showing systemic symptoms throughout
- A small green tomato visible, indicating the plant was infected early

These symptoms — particularly the **fern-leaf/shoestring distortion**, leaf narrowing, mosaic coloration, and systemic curling — are the hallmark presentation of **Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV)** in tomatoes. CMV causes severe leaf distortion, filiform leaves, and mosaic patterns. This distinguishes it from Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (which shows bronzing/necrotic ring spots) or bacterial wilts (which show vascular browning/wilting without this kind of leaf distortion).
